A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same HanDyVQA research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–E. Text, tables, figures, and equations support reliable comparison; apparent equation-extraction differences were resolved through visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original MCQ and segmentation evaluations, human assessments, ablations, and fine-tuning experiments, including Tables 3–8, 25, and 32.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds Gemini-2.5-Pro performance and error analyses across input frame counts in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, HOI-cue integration architecture, frozen encoders, and contrastive training procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same method, and Appendix D retains the same QLoRA fine-tuning approach.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Ego4D-derived HanDyVQA coverage: six MCQ categories and Objects/Object Parts segmentation tasks. The added Gemini frame-count analysis uses existing data and tasks, without introducing another domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds Gemini-2.5-Pro to the frame-count and error comparisons previously comprising Qwen2.5-VL-7B and mPLUG-Owl3-8B. Gemini already appeared in Table 3, but its participation in this particular comparison is new. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The added Gemini analysis evaluates 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64 frames at 480×854, extending its previously reported 16-frame evaluation. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training settings, and the other models' evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 and Figure 4 extend frame-count sensitivity and four-category error analysis to Gemini-2.5-Pro. Existing HOI-cue ablations, segmentation analyses, GPT-4o answerability analyses, and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies model-run seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The three-rater human averages and agreement reporting in Table 25 are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds Gemini performance and error-rate curves, with Section 4.1 reporting consistent benefits from additional frames and its lowest errors at 32 frames. Existing numerical tables are unchanged, including Table 3's 72.6% Gemini and 96.6% human average accuracies.

T1.justification: The error-rate definition, appendix frame-sampling formulas, and contrastive objective in Algorithm 1 are mathematically unchanged. Differences in extracted equation text do not represent changes to the rendered mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a benchmark covering manipulation and effects, evidence of model–human performance gaps, and benefits from explicit HOI cues. Abstract compression does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 now contrasts Gemini's stronger use of additional temporal input with open-source model limitations. Its concluding diagnosis changes from 'the models' to 'the open source models' struggling with spatial relationships and increased temporal information.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL on the title page, providing an access pointer absent from v1; the PDFs do not establish which resources that page supplies. Appendix D also changes training-cost wording to confirm execution, retaining the same single H200 and roughly two hours per category.

R1.justification: The same 60 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Updates to entries such as HOT3D, OSCAR, and FineBio concern publication metadata or titles of existing works, rather than added research references.

P1.justification: The abstract and several related-work and experimental paragraphs are shortened or polished. Typographical corrections, terminology normalization, bibliographic cleanup, and acknowledgment edits accompany these limited revisions; the section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with Gemini curves, revised legends and colors, and adjusted axis ranges. Figure 1 receives presentation corrections, and text reflow shifts section boundaries across pages. The table structures and nearly all appendix displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new Figure 4 analysis establishes how the strongest evaluated model responds to additional frames and supports a more precise distinction between Gemini and open-source temporal-processing limitations. Clearer prose and the project-page pointer provide further modest benefits. The benchmark, method, and principal results remain stable, so the overall improvement is limited.
